paragraphs.text: Zhalfir (zhal-FEER or zall-feer ) is the youngest known plane in the Multiverse and previously was a substantial portion of the continent of Jamuraa on Dominaria . For more than five thousand years Zhalfir was a militaristic kingdom on Dominaria along the western plains, forests, and coasts of Jamuraa. After being phased out to save it from Phyrexian invasion , its former location became known as the Zhalfirin Void . It became a plane of its own, and gained its own worldsoul , in the aftermath of the New Phyrexian Invasion .

Zhalfir made up the northwestern coast of Jamuraa's western continent. Its coastal sands give way to a dune forest, eventually leading to scrubland dominated by low, wide-canopied trees. Further inland, it has markets. It is bordered by low mountains on its eastern edge and by rocky plateaus on its north. Its earth is red-colored.

While phased out of Dominaria, it had no moons. Now, it is orbited by the former suns of Mirrodin . Due to the five suns orbiting Zhalfir, nightfall never occurs. Zhalfir has a spirit realm which is permanently dark, and occupied by the dead and other spirits.
The kingdom is ruled by a monarch, currently, Queen Wezna , who is advised by the kingdom's general, currently Mageta , and a council of five high wizards, one from each of Zhalfir's Creeds.
Its merchants use coins as currency.
An old Zhalfirin gesture of gratitude involves kissing one's fingers, touching them to the forehead, and placing one's hand over the heart.

Its military is organized into Sidar generals, askari soldiers, akinji irregulars, and altali, fleetfooted medics clad in bright white whose sole job it is to see bodies returned home. Its soldiers wear enchanted lizard-skin armor and war paint.

Long ruled by the royal family from its capital Ki’pamu , Zhalfir benefited from its magical strength. The Zhalfirins pioneered the five colors of mana on Dominaria and, unlike the rest of the plane, escaped the ravages of the Sylex Blast , the Ice Age , and the Flood Ages . Zhalfir possessed a large standing army (personified by the Knightly Order of Askari) but was also constantly the site of internal squabbling by its contentious and powerful noble class.

For many years, Zhalfir was the home of the great mages Teferi and Jolrael . Teferi was the counsel to the ancient kings and queens of Zhalfir. History did not record that his tenure as a court mage ended unhappily. He did not like to discuss the circumstances that led to his falling out with the king and the end of his career as a court mage.
Teferi's final act before his departure was the creation of the Creeds of Magic, originally called Guilds.

When Teferi returned some thirty years later, he found the continent on the brink of war. While Zhalfir at this time was ruled by a king, southern Zhalfir had split off and formed the theocracy of Femeref because the churches didn't agree with the fact that Teferi had left control of the dead in the hands of the Shadow Creed. When Femeref had found gold in the mountains, the northern country of Suq'Ata had invaded part of Zhalfir and had driven the dwarves there from their mountain homes. When the dwarves had aided Femeref in harvesting the gold, increasing their efficiency greatly, Zhalfir felt cheated out of their rightful portion of the gold. Teferi tracked down and tutored a capable girl of royal descent. After crowning her as Queen Yormeba , she brought peace to the nation but failed to unify it. Tired of the petty squabbles of his people, Teferi left with a group of trusted advisors, sages, artificers, and sorcerers. They sailed for a hidden realm in the Chaza Isles , where Teferi wanted to manipulate time to make it easier to summon creatures.

At the time of the Phyrexian Invasion , Zhalfir was the most advanced nation on Dominaria and was ruled by Queen Wezna . Because of its powerful magic, technology, and military, Urza intended it to take the brunt of the attack. The leaders of Zhalfir thought they would triumph, but Teferi thought otherwise. He phased out Zhalfir alongside parts of northwestern Jamuraa because he wanted to spare it from the horrors of the Phyrexian assault.

When Teferi reappeared on Dominaria three hundred years later, he found the plane torn apart by temporal fissures and rifts . To prevent the plane's destruction, he had to find a way to close the temporal rifts created by cataclysmic events in the past. Two major rifts had been created by his phasing of Zhalfir and Shiv. He managed to close the Shivan rift by sacrificing his planeswalker spark.

The Zhalfirin Rift suffered a different fate. Jeska , manipulated by Leshrac , used Radha as a mana lens, forcefully closing the Zhalfirin rift without realizing the consequence of her actions. Without precise timing, the phased lands of Zhalfir were lost seemingly forever, cast into oblivion, although Teferi said that he could probably save it if he was still a planeswalker. The legacy of the Zhalfirin culture partially lives on in the nations of Femeref and Suq'Ata .
Over three hundred years after the kingdom was phased out when Teferi met the planeswalker Wrenn , she explained how he could unravel his spells and promised to help him with returning Zhalfir.

When Teferi was disconnected from the Temporal Anchor in his search for answers to the looming New Phyrexian Invasion , he ended up in Zhalfir, realizing that only a decade had passed there and that the Zhalfirans were still preparing for the first Phyrexian Invasion of Dominaria . He discovered that The Wanderer had been able to reach the land as well, indicating that it had become a pocket plane . He reconnected with Sidar Jabari and Queen Wezna and found that Kaervek had escaped his Amber Prison . It gave him a new resolve to battle the Phyrexians. Wrenn would find Zhalfir once she bonded with Realmbreaker during the New Phyrexian Invasion, reuniting it with the rest of the multiverse and allowing the Zhalfirin army a way to attack and combat the Phyrexian forces on New Phyrexia .

Wrenn and Realmbreaker swapped New Phyrexia's and Zhalfir's places in the Multiverse , allowing Zhalfir to become a plane of its own. Due to the merging only affecting the landmass of each plane, the sky of New Phyrexia remained in place and Mirrodin's five suns now orbit Zhalfir. The survivors of Mirrodin have been welcomed into the new plane as refugees, having evacuated through the Omenpath that Wrenn opened between Zhalfir and New Phyrexia.
Locations in Zhalfir ( 45 cards ):

Lake Albiuto - an ancient, rock-bound lake Albiuto - a lakeshore settlement in the mountains, eight leagues from Sidar Kondo 's village. Albiuto was where Vuel once sold items of the Legacy after stealing them from his foster-brother, Gerrard Capashen .
Buleusi Bay and the Buleusi Coast Chaza Isles - a small archipelago off the coast Teferi's Isle - site of Teferi 's laboratory, which was infamously phased out for 200 years.
Daraja Plains - formerly neutral ground between Zhalfir and Femeref
The Desert of Bones - a dune desert with a caravan road leading to Ki'pamu
Kiingal - a large port city in the north
Ki'pamu - the capital and royal city of Zhalfir Leather Street - a poor area of ramshackle cottages The Nobles' Quarter - home of Ki'pamu's elite

Mtenda plains - Zhalfir's heartlands, where its peoples' crops are grown. Ntatsu Plains Kenlo - a village on the plains Mbutu Tree Monkey Tree Watering Hole - an oasis where many animals come to drink
Mwonvuli Jungle - a sprawling jungle, home of Jolrael . The Mwonvuli Delta - where Kaervek imprisoned Mangara in the Amber Prison .
Port City - the seaside harbor town where Crovax joined the crew of the Skyship Weatherlight .
The Talruum Mountains - a rugged range, home to minotaurs
The Teremko Mountains - tall peaks, home to griffins
Ufunguo - the first city to fall to Kaervek in the Mirage War
The Uktabi Jungle - a small, southern jungle Salamzuri - a city built by Quirion elves
Unyaro Jungle - a jungle plagued by bees
Unyaro Plains - a land of griffins
Uuserk Marshes - inhospitable quagmires Aku - tomb city, the domain of Shauku
The five suns of Mirrodin : Bringer , the Eye of Doom , Ingle , the Sky Tyrant , and Lyese .

The name of Zhalfir is derived from Khalfani, a Swahili name meaning "destined to rule". For the return set Zhalfir , R&D explored the Afrofantasy genre. They wanted an Afrocentric story that was fantasy-based, and found that there were not a lot of beaten paths. In developing the set, the team was careful not to pull from just one subsection of Afrofantasy culture, but to instead include different interpretations from around the continent and the world. It contains elements from the Caribbean, North Africa, Egypt, etc.
